text:
Maria G: heads-up — canary for galsim-4b-microq is spiking on structured funcall parses in the eval harness, about ~12% failures vs 0.7% on fp baseline. samples attached below.

Tom R: hmm. is this happening during streaming boundary truncation or full responses? any raw model outputs?

Maria G: mostly full responses from the canary logs. here's a typical failure we see (copied verbatim from the model stream):

Maria G: ```
{
  \"response\": \"{\\\"tool_call\\\":\\\"invoke\\\",\\\"args\\\":\\\"{\\\\\\\"query_id\\\\\\\":123,\\\\\\\"term\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"name\\\\\\\"}\\\"}\" 
}
```

Maria G: the nested JSON is double-encoded — instead of returning an object for args the model emits a string containing escaped JSON. parser treats it as invalid schema.

Kevin L: that screams tokenization/serialization mismatch after quantization. microquant pack seems to change how quotes/backslashes are emitted in mid-sequence. did you try lowering temp / adjusting stop sequences?

Maria G: lowered temp from 0.8 -> 0.2 in a quick run — parse failures dropped to ~3% but outputs became conservative and occasionally omitted optional fields.

Priya S: important note: our retry logic triggers when parse fails, and the toolchain re-invokes the function. I'm seeing duplicated external calls in traces — leads to duplicate side effects for non-idempotent APIs. we should treat that as high priority.

Tom R: can we reproduce deterministically with a fixed prompt + seed? need to know if it's sampling noise or systematic serialization bias.

Maria G: yes, reduced test to a 2k-sample deterministic seed run on the canary model and still saw ~10% double-escaped args. pushing a minimal repro to the eval job: /link-to-run (internal).

Kevin L: quick mitigation: postprocess step that attempts to json_unescape string fields when schema expects an object. regex hack: if value matches ^\"\{.*\}\"$ then unescape and parse. not ideal but low-risk for canary. also we should prefer the model to emit objects by nudging the few-shot: show examples with unquoted objects in toolcall fields.

Priya S: longer-term we need two changes: 1) change retry policy to verify idempotency or dedupe by request id before invoking external side-effecting calls; 2) add telemetry: funcall_parse_failures, funcall_retry_count, funcall_duplicate_side_effects. correlate with model variant, quant level, and temperature.

Maria G: proposal for AB canary: three arms — (A) no-retry (fail-fast) + metric capture, (B) lenient-unescape postproc + current retry, (C) low-temp + explicit stop/seps + stricter prompt examples. run 50k eval prompts each, track parse_fail_rate, duplicate_calls, and semantic fidelity.

Tom R: sounds good. define owners & timeline. Maria you own arm B postproc & telemetry; Kevin you own prompting and temp sweep for arm C; Priya you own retry/dedupe change and ops telemetry. I'll coordinate the canary rollout and safety gates. target: start next Monday, end of week validation.

canary-bot: deploy event — canary/galsim-4b-microq started at 2024-05-13T09:12:01Z

sre-bot: noticed spike in 5xx errors around canary warmup window, alert threshold reached — paging oncall.

Kevin L: one more note — some earlier logs show the model emitting explicit \`\"args\": { ... }\` for the same prompt when run with fp. so this is a quantization artifact, not prompt ambiguity. worth a quick kernel/quant config diff.

Maria G: will attach side-by-side token-level diff and a few representative samples to the canary ticket. also adding gating rule: if duplicate_calls > 0.5% we abort.

Priya S: I'll add a lightweight dedupe proxy layer for the external function calls so we can tolerate small retry rates safely during the experiment.

Tom R: great — update the canary ticket with run ids and I'll review the telemetry dashboards after first 5k requests. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
